newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark defends Labour's economic policies.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark defends Labour's economic policies.

text.p: Labour leader Helen Clark on Wednesday hit back at New Zealand First criticism of her party's economic policies, saying modest surpluses were planned for the rest of the decade, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
NZ First leader Winston Peters said on Tuesday that Labour's figures did not "stack up" and there were problems "with regard to fiscal spending".
But Clark said Peters "should get a new financial analyst".
She said Labour policies would see a budget surplus of NZ$2 billion in 1997-98, and $1.5 billion and $2.5 billion in the years following.
"In my view that is a quite an adequate cushion," she told Newstalk ZB radio.
"It enables us to proceed slowly but deliberately with very important public spending proposals, and also enables us to keep a modest rate of debt repayment."
Clark reiterated that Labour's top tax rate would be no higher than 39 percent.
"That is our policy and we do not propose to vary from the policy," she said.
She added that she was prepared to work with Peters to form a coalition government despite their differences.
"I haven't worked with Mr Peters before; he comes from a different political tradition," she said.
"All I can say is that this new system requires us to work with people we haven't worked with before and in the interests of New Zealand I'm prepared to give it my very best shot."
